JAMF_DEVICE_TYPE.description: Selects which Jamf Pro surfaces the executor walks. Valid values: 'computer' (walks the Classic API GET /JSSResource/computers list plus the modern Jamf Pro API GET /api/v1/computers-inventory paginated walk, de-duplicated by id so the richer modern record wins when both surfaces return the same computer), 'mobile' (walks the Classic API GET /JSSResource/mobiledevices list — iOS / iPadOS / tvOS records), or 'both' (the default; walks all three surfaces so a fresh playbook pulls the full Apple fleet without further config). Whitespace is trimmed and the value is lowercased so operator typos like 'Computer' / 'MOBILE' round-trip correctly. Invalid values fall back to 'both' with a warning rather than aborting (the dispatcher tolerates operator typos here because computer / mobile are the only narrowing knobs and walking too much is preferable to walking nothing). Default 'both'.

name: jamf_pro
title: Jamf Pro
description: Jamf Pro asset-inventory importer. Pulls managed Apple endpoints (macOS computers + iOS / iPadOS / tvOS mobile devices) from a Jamf Pro tenant and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON. Jamf Pro is the MDM authority of record for the Apple fleet, so this executor is the CMDB-class feed Faraday operators correlate the EDR / vuln-scanner agents' findings against to confirm an exposed host is a known managed Apple endpoint. Each Jamf Pro computer becomes one Faraday host (the modern Jamf Pro API's general.lastIpAddress — with general.lastReportedIp as a fallback — projects onto host.ip; loopback / 0.0.0.0 / ::1 are explicitly skipped and the executor falls back to the 0.0.0.0 sentinel when nothing usable is found; the general.name / hardware.serialNumber / hardware.modelIdentifier projection lands on host.hostnames; hardware.macAddress with hardware.altMacAddress fallback lands on host.mac; and the operatingSystem.name / operatingSystem.version / operatingSystem.build / hardware.model chain joins onto host.os). Each Jamf Pro mobile device becomes one Faraday host keyed on the ip_address / wifi_ip field when present (mobile devices CAN expose their last-known IP under the Classic API's mobile-device record) or the 0.0.0.0 sentinel otherwise; the name / device_name / udid projection lands on host.hostnames, wifi_mac_address lands on host.mac, and the model / model_display / model_identifier chain joins onto host.os. The asset itself becomes one Faraday vulnerability with the [ASSET-INVENTORY] engine prefix so the data lands in the Faraday workspace alongside the other CMDB-class feeds (Axonius, Device42, Fleet, runZero, Armis, Jira Insight). Endpoints used: GET /JSSResource/computers (the Jamf Pro Classic API's lightweight computer list — records are deliberately thin (only id + name) because the Classic API expects operators to walk each id separately via /JSSResource/computers/id/N for full detail; we use the Classic list as a belt-and-suspenders fallback for tenants where the modern API hasn't been enabled and de-dup against the modern walk via the shared id key), GET /api/v1/computers-inventory?page=N&page-size=100&section=GENERAL&section=HARDWARE&section=OPERATING_SYSTEM&section=USER_AND_LOCATION (the modern Jamf Pro API's full computer inventory; returns {totalCount: N, results: [...]} with each record carrying id, udid plus the requested sections — the dispatcher always requests the same four sections so the field projection is deterministic), and GET /JSSResource/mobiledevices (the Jamf Pro Classic API's mobile-device list; returns {mobile_devices: [{id, name, device_name, udid, wifi_mac_address, serial_number, model, model_identifier, model_display, username}]} — the Classic API IS rich enough here because mobile records historically don't carry the same depth as computer records, so a single list call is the canonical mobile walk). JAMF_DEVICE_TYPE selects which surfaces to walk (computer -> Classic /computers + modern /computers-inventory; mobile -> Classic /mobiledevices; both -> all three). Pagination is per-surface: /api/v1/computers-inventory is page-based (page + page-size, 0-indexed) and walked page-by-page until len(results) < page-size or JAMF_PAGES (env-only override, default 5, clamped to [1, 50]) is reached; page-size is fixed at 100 (Jamf Pro's documented default). The Classic API list endpoints don't paginate — they return the whole tenant's records in a single call — so we issue one GET per Classic surface and walk the returned list directly. Severity is always info because Jamf Pro hits are MDM inventory entries, not vulnerability findings — operators correlate against the other agents' findings via the Jamf-Id / Jamf-Udid / Jamf-Serial / Jamf-Model / Jamf-Platform / Jamf-LastContact / Jamf-User / Jamf-Department / Jamf-Building / Jamf-Site refs on computer hits, and the Jamf-Id / Jamf-Udid / Jamf-Serial / Jamf-Model / Jamf-User / Jamf-Type refs on mobile hits. Auth: Jamf Pro uses OAuth2 client-credentials. Operators register an API role + client in the Jamf Pro console under Settings -> System -> API roles and clients to obtain JAMF_CLIENT_ID + JAMF_CLIENT_SECRET. On every executor run the dispatcher POSTs client_id=<id>&client_secret=<secret>&grant_type=client_credentials form data to /api/oauth/token and pulls the short-lived access token out of the access_token field. The token travels on every subsequent /JSSResource/ or /api/v1/ request as the standard Authorization: Bearer <token> header. JAMF_HOST is the operator's Jamf Pro tenant host (e.g. mycorp.jamfcloud.com); on-prem Jamf Pro deployments are tolerated and https:// is added automatically when the operator pasted in a bare FQDN. Tags: [jamf_pro, asset-inventory, computer|mobile].
